# Unused, dormant and generated file audit

[简体中文](unused-code-audit.zh-CN.md)

Audit date: **2026-10-22**

This file marks material that is unnecessary to the current runtime without pretending that every unreachable source file is garbage. It is an annotation and cleanup guide only; the audit did not delete project files.

> **Execution note (2026-10-22):** the two accidental Claude probe files are now absent. `coverage/` and `dist/` remain local regeneratable output and are still shown by `packaging/windows/cleanup-local.ps1` in preview mode. No production source file is currently marked `DELETE-SAFE`.

## Labels

| Label | Meaning | Default action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DELETE-SAFE` | Temporary or generated local material with no source, test-fixture or release-authority role | Delete when convenient |
| `REGENERATABLE` | Build, coverage or dependency output recreated by a documented command | Keep out of source control; regenerate when needed |
| `STALE-ARTIFACT` | Generated output that no longer represents the same source revision as the rest of the workspace | Do not run or publish; remove before a clean build |
| `DORMANT-CODE` | Tested implementation with no call from a current production entry point | Keep until the named integration decision/task is completed |
| `TEST-COMPAT` | Used by tests, upgrade promises or historical compatibility, but not by normal runtime | Keep unless the compatibility promise is intentionally removed |
| `ACTIVE` | Required by a build, package, runtime path or current documented workflow | Keep |

## Method and evidence boundary

The audit used:

- `package.json`, `tsdown.config.ts`, Go module metadata and packaging scripts to identify entry points;
- `go list ./...` to inspect package imports;
- repository-wide reference searches excluding tests to find production callers;
- a current `go build ./cmd/errkb` and symbol inspection as supporting evidence;
- local file sizes and the previously verified behavior differences between the source, root `dist`, installed EXE and `dist/release` EXE.

The production entry points are `src/index.ts` for the DSH package and `cmd/errkb` for the Go program. An exported Go function is not considered active merely because it compiles or has tests; it needs a production caller or an external package contract. Conversely, a test fixture is not called garbage merely because the executable does not load it.

## B. Stale output that should be replaced as a unit

| Path | Label | Why it is unsafe now | Correct treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dist/errkb.exe` and root installer/checksum/resource files | `STALE-ARTIFACT` | Built at a different implementation point from the release subdirectory; the binary does not expose the local Web route | Remove before rebuilding from a tagged commit |
| `dist/release/errkb-0.1.0/` | `STALE-ARTIFACT` | Old release bundle; its EXE has a different command surface from the root EXE and current source | Archive externally only if historical evidence is needed; otherwise delete locally |
| Whole `dist/` directory | `REGENERATABLE` | Ignored local build output; it is not release authority | Regenerate when needed; use the v0.1.1 GitHub Release for distribution |

Do not preserve selected binaries from these directories and combine them with newly generated installer files. The next accepted release must generate EXE, installer, manifest, SBOM and checksums from the same tagged commit.

## C. Local caches, not garbage code

| Path | Label | Role | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `node_modules/` | `REGENERATABLE` | Local dependency installation, about 119 MB | May be deleted to reclaim space; restore with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` |
| `lib/` | `ACTIVE` | Published DSH bundle; `package.json.exports` and `files` point to it | Keep for package/store review; regenerate with `pnpm build` when source changes |
| `lib/index.js.map` | `REGENERATABLE` | Local sourcemap ignored by `.gitignore` | Optional locally; do not treat `lib/index.js` or `lib/index.d.ts` the same way |

## D. Previously dormant code — reconciled 2026-10-22

Most items from the original audit are now production-reachable and must not be removed:

| Area and paths | Current production path | Label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detail/settings/stats models and edit service | `internal/webshell` → daemon API/backend → `NewDetailService`, stats, audit and settings | `ACTIVE` |
| Generic log tailer | `errkb tail --file` → `cmd/errkb/tail.go` → `capture.NewTailer` | `ACTIVE` |
| Legacy Markdown exchange | `errkb markdown import|export` → `cmd/errkb/markdown.go` | `ACTIVE` + `TEST-COMPAT` |
| PostgreSQL manager and backup/upgrade helpers | `errkb pg` → `service.NewPGManager`; `postgres.ps1` is now only the installer argument adapter | `ACTIVE` |

The remaining genuinely dormant pair is `internal/ui/notify.go` plus `internal/service/notifications.go`: both are tested, but no production path constructs `NewNoticeService` or `NewNotification`. Keep them as `DORMANT-CODE` until desktop notification delivery is either connected or explicitly removed from scope. Do not treat the now-wired UI, tail, Markdown or PostgreSQL code as cleanup candidates.

## F. Active code that should not be removed

- `src/`: every TypeScript module is reachable from the `src/index.ts` DSH bundle import graph.
- `cmd/errkb/`: command dispatch and all currently exposed CLI modes.
- `internal/core/`, `internal/redact/`, `internal/contract/`: shared deterministic processing and contracts.
- Active database retrieval/recording/migration files in `internal/database/` and `db/migrations/`.
- `internal/service/api.go`, `backend.go`, `client.go`, `daemon.go`, `doctor.go`, `pipe.go`, `queue.go`, `search_api.go`.
- `internal/ui/status.go`, `tray.go`, `omnibox.go`, `omnibox_win.go`.
- `internal/mcp/` and `internal/webshell/`.
- `packaging/windows/`: produces, installs and tests the Windows artifact; WF-011A/WF-011B exercise its lifecycle and recovery.

## Recommended cleanup order

Preview the exact confirmed targets with:

```powershell
pwsh -File packaging/windows/cleanup-local.ps1
```

After reviewing the four target groups, apply the cleanup with:

```powershell
pwsh -File packaging/windows/cleanup-local.ps1 -Apply
```

1. Delete the two accidental Claude probe files.
2. Clear `coverage/` and the four explicit `dist` scratch/helper areas in section A.
3. Treat the rest of `dist/` as invalid and rebuild it only after a real Git worktree and one target commit exist.
4. Keep the wired Web UI, tailer, Markdown and PostgreSQL manager code; their production entry points now exist.
5. Decide separately whether to connect or remove the still-dormant desktop notification model/service.
6. Completed: the four superseded local EKB cards were removed and WF-012 was closed after the verified v0.1.1 release.

## Deletion gate

A source file may move from `DORMANT-CODE` to `DELETE-SAFE` only when all of the following are true:

- repository-wide production references are zero;
- no public package export, CLI command, installer step or compatibility promise requires it;
- the corresponding implementation-plan task is removed or replaced;
- tests and fixtures are removed or redirected intentionally, not merely broken;
- both language versions of feature, status and implementation documentation are updated;
- Go tests, TypeScript tests/typecheck, CUE validation and packaging checks still pass.

This gate prevents “cleanup” from deleting code that is merely waiting to be connected.
